# Employee Salary Structure in India Explained: Basic Pay, HRA, DA, Allowances, and Deductions (2026 Guide)


October 13, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/employee-salary-structure-in-india-explained-basic-pay-hra-da-allowances-and-deductions-2026-guide/#respond)


If you have ever looked at your offer letter and wondered why your CTC says ₹6 lakh but your bank only receives ₹38,000 every month, you are not alone. The gap between CTC and take home salary confuses millions of Indian employees and business owners every year.


The reason is simple: an Indian salary is not one number. It is a structure made up of more than a dozen components, each with its own tax treatment, legal requirement, and calculation formula. Basic pay, HRA, dearness allowance, special allowance, conveyance, PF, ESI, professional tax, TDS, and gratuity all play different roles in how much you earn and how much you actually receive.


For employers, designing the right salary structure is equally important. A poorly structured salary can increase your PF and gratuity costs by lakhs every year. A well structured one keeps you compliant with labour laws while maximizing your employee’s take home pay.


This guide explains every single salary component in India, shows you how each one is calculated, and provides ready to use salary structures at three different CTC levels. Whether you are an employee trying to understand your payslip or a business owner designing salary structures for your team, this is the only reference you need.


## What Is a Salary Structure?


A salary structure is the detailed breakdown of an employee’s total compensation into individual components. Each component serves a specific purpose: some are fixed, some vary with performance, some are taxable, and some offer tax savings.


### The Three Layers of Indian Salary


Layer What It Includes Who Sees It


CTC (Cost to Company) Everything the employer spends: gross salary + employer PF + ESI + gratuity + insurance + training Mentioned in the offer letter and appraisal letter


Gross Salary All earnings before deductions: basic + HRA + all allowances + variable pay Appears on the salary slip (earnings side)


Net Salary (Take Home) The amount credited to the employee’s bank account after all deductions What actually reaches the bank


### How CTC, Gross, and Net Salary Relate


Step What Happens Example (₹6 LPA CTC)


Start with CTC Annual cost the company bears ₹6,00,000 per year


Remove employer PF (12% of Basic) Employer’s PF contribution is part of CTC but not your gross ₹28,800


Remove employer ESI (3.25% of gross, if applicable) Employer ESI is part of CTC ₹0 (not applicable if gross above ₹21,000/month)


Remove gratuity provision (4.81% of Basic) Accrued annually, paid after 5 years ₹11,544


Remove other employer costs Insurance, EDLI, admin charges ₹6,000


**= Annual Gross Salary** **₹5,53,656**


Monthly Gross Salary Gross / 12 ₹46,138


Minus Employee PF 12% of Basic deducted from employee ₹2,400


Minus Professional Tax State tax ₹200


Minus TDS Income tax on projected income ₹600


**= Monthly Net Salary** **₹42,938**


The difference between ₹50,000 monthly CTC and ₹42,938 take home is not “lost” money. It goes toward your retirement (PF), insurance (ESI), future benefit (gratuity), and taxes.


For a detailed calculation with step by step examples, read our[CTC to in hand salary calculation guide](https://salarybox.in/blog/how-to-calculate-in-hand-salary-from-ctc-india/) .


## Every Earnings Component Explained in Detail


Let us now go through every component that appears on the earnings side of your salary.


### 1. Basic Salary (Basic Pay)


Basic salary is the foundation of your entire salary structure. Almost every other component is calculated as a percentage of basic.


Aspect Details


Definition The core fixed component of salary, excluding all allowances and bonuses


Typical range 40% to 50% of CTC


Tax treatment Fully taxable under both old and new tax regimes


Legal minimum Under the Code on Wages, 2019: Basic + DA must be at least 50% of total remuneration


#### Why Basic Salary Percentage Matters So Much


Basic salary is the base for calculating several statutory benefits. A higher basic means higher employer costs but also higher employee benefits:


Statutory Benefit Calculated On Impact of Higher Basic


PF (Provident Fund) 12% of Basic + DA Higher retirement savings, but higher deduction from salary


Gratuity 15/26 × Basic × Years of service Higher gratuity payout after 5 years


HRA tax exemption Percentage of Basic Higher HRA exemption reduces taxable income


Leave encashment Basic / 30 × Unused leave days Higher encashment value


Bonus (under Bonus Act) 8.33% to 20% of Basic + DA Higher bonus amount


#### The 50% Basic Pay Rule (Code on Wages, 2019)


The Code on Wages, 2019 introduced a significant change to salary structuring in India:


Aspect Old Practice New Rule


Basic + DA percentage Many companies kept it at 30% to 40% to reduce PF cost Must be at least 50% of total remuneration


What counts as “wages” Narrowly defined Broadly defined: includes basic, DA, and retaining allowance


Allowances exceeding 50% Could be structured freely The excess gets reclassified as “wages” for PF/gratuity purposes


Non cash benefits (food, accommodation) No cap Counted toward wages only up to 15% of total wages


**Example of How the 50% Rule Works:**


Scenario Before (Non Compliant) After (Compliant)


Monthly CTC ₹60,000 ₹60,000


Basic + DA ₹18,000 (30%) ₹30,000 (50%)


HRA ₹12,000 ₹15,000


Special Allowance ₹22,000 ₹7,000


Other Allowances ₹8,000 ₹8,000


Employee PF (12% of Basic) ₹2,160 ₹3,600


Employer PF (12% of Basic) ₹2,160 ₹3,600


Impact on employer Lower PF cost Higher PF cost (+₹1,440/month per employee)


Impact on employee Lower take home (slightly) Higher retirement savings


**Current Status:** The major provisions of the Code on Wages came into effect on November 21, 2025. Employers are advised to align salary structures for FY 2026-27 and beyond.


### 2. House Rent Allowance (HRA)


HRA is the second largest component in most salary structures and offers significant tax savings under the old tax regime.


Aspect Details


Definition An allowance paid to employees to cover rental accommodation expenses


Typical range 40% to 50% of Basic salary


Metro city rate 50% of Basic (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad)


Non metro rate 40% of Basic


Tax treatment Partially exempt under Section 10(13A) (old regime only); fully taxable under new regime


#### HRA Tax Exemption Formula


The exempt amount is the lowest of three calculations:


Calculation Formula


Option A Actual HRA received from employer


Option B 50% of Basic + DA (metro) or 40% (non metro)


Option C Actual rent paid minus 10% of Basic + DA


**Worked Example:**


Detail Value


Monthly Basic ₹25,000


Monthly HRA received ₹12,500


City Pune (metro)


Monthly rent paid ₹15,000


Option Calculation Amount


A (Actual HRA) As received ₹12,500


B (50% of Basic) ₹25,000 × 50% ₹12,500


C (Rent minus 10% of Basic) ₹15,000 minus ₹2,500 ₹12,500


Exempt HRA = ₹12,500 (lowest of the three). In this case, the entire HRA is exempt.


**If the employee pays only ₹8,000 rent:**


Option Amount


A ₹12,500


B ₹12,500


C ₹8,000 minus ₹2,500 = ₹5,500


Exempt HRA = ₹5,500. Taxable HRA = ₹12,500 minus ₹5,500 = ₹7,000


**Requirements for Claiming HRA Exemption:**


Requirement Details


Rent receipts Must submit monthly or quarterly receipts


Landlord PAN Required if annual rent exceeds ₹1,00,000


Family rent (from April 2026) Must disclose on Form 124 if paying rent to a family member


Actual rent payment proof Bank transfer records strengthen the claim


Self owned house HRA exemption not available if you live in your own house in the same city


### 3. Dearness Allowance (DA)


Aspect Details


Definition An inflation adjustment allowance linked to the Consumer Price Index (CPI)


Where it is common Central and state government employees, public sector undertakings, and some unionized private companies


Private sector Most private companies do not include DA separately; inflation adjustments are handled through annual salary revisions


Current rate (central government) Approximately 55% of Basic Pay (revised twice a year, in January and July)


Tax treatment Fully taxable


PF impact DA is added to Basic for PF calculation (PF = 12% of Basic + DA)


**Important for Private Sector Employers:** Under the Code on Wages, 2019, the “wages” definition includes Basic + DA. If your company does not pay DA, then Basic alone must meet the 50% threshold.


### 4. Special Allowance


Aspect Details


Definition A balancing component that fills the gap between fixed components (Basic, HRA, etc.) and total gross salary


Typical range 15% to 35% of CTC, depending on how much goes to other components


Tax treatment Fully taxable under both tax regimes


PF applicability Not included in PF calculation (unless the company voluntarily includes it)


Why it exists Gives employers flexibility to adjust the overall salary structure without changing fixed percentages


**Calculation:** Special Allowance = Gross Salary minus Basic minus HRA minus all other fixed allowances


This is the component employers adjust when they need to change the salary structure without affecting statutory calculations.


### 5. Conveyance Allowance (Transport Allowance)


Aspect Details


Definition A fixed allowance to cover daily commute expenses


Old exemption (pre FY 2018-19) ₹1,600 per month was tax exempt


Current status The old exemption has been replaced by the ₹75,000 standard deduction (effective from AY 2025-26 under both regimes)


Differently abled employees ₹3,200 per month remains exempt


Why it still appears Many companies continue to show it as a separate line item for transparency, even though it carries no special tax benefit now


### 6. Leave Travel Allowance (LTA)


Aspect Details


Definition An allowance for travel expenses during approved leave


Exemption rule Exempt for actual travel costs within India, 2 journeys in a block of 4 years


Current block January 2026 to December 2029


What is covered Travel fare only (train, flight, bus). Hotel, food, and local transport are not covered


Tax treatment Exempt under Section 10(5) in the old regime; fully taxable under the new regime


Proof required Travel tickets and boarding passes


### 7. Medical Allowance


Aspect Details


Old exemption ₹15,000 per year was tax exempt


Current status Fully taxable since FY 2018-19; replaced by the standard deduction


Common practice Many companies have merged medical allowance into the special allowance component


### 8. Other Allowances You May See


Allowance Purpose Tax Treatment Typical Amount


Children Education Allowance Children’s school fees Exempt: ₹100/month per child, max 2 children (old regime) ₹200/month


Hostel Expenditure Allowance Children’s boarding school costs Exempt: ₹300/month per child, max 2 children (old regime) ₹600/month


Meal Vouchers (Sodexo/Zeta) Food and meal expenses Exempt up to ₹50 per meal (approximately ₹2,200/month for 22 working days, 2 meals) ₹2,200/month


Telephone/Internet Reimbursement Work related communication Exempt up to ₹15,000/year with bills ₹1,250/month


Fuel Reimbursement Official travel by personal vehicle Exempt with fuel bills (for official use) Varies


Uniform Allowance Official work attire Exempt with purchase bills Varies


Books and Periodicals Professional reading material Exempt up to ₹10,000/year with bills ₹833/month


Shift Allowance Night or rotating shift compensation Fully taxable ₹500 to ₹3,000/month


City Compensatory Allowance Cost of living adjustment for expensive cities Fully taxable ₹500 to ₹2,000/month


**Note on Reimbursements:** Tax exemption on reimbursements requires actual bills. If the employee does not submit bills, the amount becomes taxable. Employers must maintain proper documentation of all reimbursement claims.


## Every Deduction Component Explained


These are the amounts subtracted from your gross salary before the net pay reaches your bank account.


### 1. Employee Provident Fund (EPF)


Aspect Details


Rate 12% of Basic + DA


Statutory wage ceiling ₹15,000 per month (employers can voluntarily compute on higher basic)


Applicability Mandatory for establishments with 20 or more employees


Tax benefit Deductible under Section 80C up to ₹1,50,000 per year (old regime)


Interest rate (2025-26) 8.25% per annum (set by EPFO annually)


**Where Your PF Money Goes:**


Component Rate Description


Employee contribution to EPF 12% of Basic + DA Goes entirely to the employee’s PF account


Employer contribution to EPF 3.67% of Basic + DA Goes to the employee’s PF account


Employer contribution to EPS 8.33% of Basic + DA (capped at ₹15,000) Goes to the Employee Pension Scheme


Employer EDLI 0.50% of Basic + DA Employee Deposit Linked Insurance (death benefit)


Employer Admin Charges 0.50% of Basic + DA EPFO administrative cost


**PF Calculation Example:**


Scenario PF on ₹15,000 ceiling PF on actual Basic (₹30,000)


Employee PF (12%) ₹1,800 ₹3,600


Employer PF (3.67%) ₹550 ₹1,101


Employer EPS (8.33%) ₹1,250 ₹1,250 (capped at ₹15,000 basic)


Total monthly PF savings ₹3,600 ₹5,951


Most private companies offer the choice between restricted PF (on ₹15,000) and unrestricted PF (on full basic). Restricted PF gives higher take home; unrestricted PF builds a larger retirement corpus.


For understanding PF applicability thresholds, read our[guide to minimum employees for PF, ESI, gratuity, and bonus](https://salarybox.in/blog/minimum-employees-pf-esi-gratuity-bonus-india/) .


### 2. Employee State Insurance (ESI)


Aspect Details


Employee rate 0.75% of gross salary


Employer rate 3.25% of gross salary


Salary threshold Applicable only if gross monthly salary is ₹21,000 or below


Establishment threshold 10 or more employees (20 in some states)


Benefits Medical treatment, sickness benefit, maternity benefit, disability benefit


**Key Point:** ESI deduction stops when an employee’s gross salary crosses ₹21,000. This happens from the next contribution period (April or October). Once ESI stops, many employers add group health insurance as an alternative benefit.


### 3. Professional Tax (PT)


Aspect Details


What it is A state government tax on income from employment or profession


Constitutional cap Maximum ₹2,500 per year


Applicability Only in states that levy PT


Tax deductibility Fully deductible from taxable income under Section 16(iii)


**State Wise PT Overview:**


Category States


PT applicable (monthly deduction) Maharashtra, Karnataka, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Odisha, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Jharkhand, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Sikkim, Mizoram


PT not applicable Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Goa, Manipur, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh


**Sample PT Slabs (Maharashtra):**


Monthly Gross Salary Monthly PT


Up to ₹7,500 Nil


₹7,501 to ₹10,000 ₹175


Above ₹10,000 ₹200 (₹300 in February to round off annual total to ₹2,500)


### 4. TDS (Tax Deducted at Source)


Aspect Details


Legal basis Section 192 of the Income Tax Act


How it works Employer estimates annual taxable income, calculates total tax, and deducts it equally across 12 months


Default regime (from AY 2024-25) New Tax Regime (employee must specifically opt out to choose old regime)


**New Tax Regime Slabs (AY 2026-27):**


Annual Taxable Income Rate


Up to ₹4,00,000 Nil


₹4,00,001 to ₹8,00,000 5%


₹8,00,001 to ₹12,00,000 10%


₹12,00,001 to ₹16,00,000 15%


₹16,00,001 to ₹20,00,000 20%


₹20,00,001 to ₹24,00,000 25%


Above ₹24,00,000 30%


Standard deduction: ₹75,000. Rebate under Section 87A makes income up to approximately ₹12,75,000 tax free.


**Old Tax Regime Slabs (AY 2026-27):**


Annual Taxable Income Rate


Up to ₹2,50,000 Nil


₹2,50,001 to ₹5,00,000 5%


₹5,00,001 to ₹10,00,000 20%


Above ₹10,00,000 30%


Standard deduction: ₹50,000. Additional deductions: Section 80C (₹1,50,000), Section 80D (₹25,000 to ₹1,00,000), HRA exemption, home loan interest (Section 24), and others.


### 5. Other Possible Deductions


Deduction What It Is When It Appears


Salary advance recovery Repayment of advance taken by employee Monthly installment until fully repaid


Loan EMI Company loan repayment Fixed monthly deduction


Loss of Pay (LOP) Deduction for unapproved absence (Daily salary × Absent days)


NPS employee contribution Voluntary National Pension System contribution Fixed amount or percentage


Group insurance premium (employee share) Employee’s share of health or life insurance Monthly or annual deduction


Canteen charges Subsidized meal facility deduction Small fixed amount


## Employer Side Components (Not Deducted from Employee)


These costs are borne by the employer and are part of CTC but do not appear as deductions on the employee’s salary slip.


Component Rate or Amount Calculation Base Purpose


Employer PF contribution 12% (split: 3.67% EPF + 8.33% EPS) Basic + DA Employee retirement savings


EDLI (Employer Deposit Linked Insurance) 0.50% Basic + DA Life insurance for employee (up to ₹7 lakh)


PF Admin Charges 0.50% Basic + DA EPFO administration


Employer ESI 3.25% Gross salary (if ≤ ₹21,000) Employee health insurance


Gratuity provision 4.81% Basic + DA Long service benefit (paid after 5 years)


Group Health Insurance ₹3,000 to ₹25,000 per employee per year Per employee Health coverage for employee and family


Group Term Life Insurance ₹500 to ₹3,000 per employee per year Per employee Death benefit


### Gratuity: The Hidden Benefit


Aspect Details


Formula (15 × Last drawn Basic + DA × Years of service) / 26


Simplified formula 4.81% of Basic + DA per year of service


Eligibility 5 years of continuous service (proposed reduction to 1 year under new code for fixed term employees)


Tax exemption Up to ₹25,00,000 (raised from ₹20 lakh in recent years)


Applicability Establishments with 10 or more employees


**Gratuity Calculation Example:** Basic + DA = ₹30,000, Years of service = 8 years Gratuity = (15 × ₹30,000 × 8) / 26 = ₹1,38,462


For more on the total cost employers bear beyond salary, read our[complete cost of hiring guide](https://salarybox.in/blog/cost-of-hiring-employee-india-2026-complete-breakdown/) .


## Complete Salary Structures at Three CTC Levels


Here are ready to use salary structures for three common CTC ranges in India, designed to be compliant with the 50% basic rule.

**Typical Role:** Delivery associate, office boy, data entry operator, field executive


Component Monthly Amount Type


**Earnings**

HRA (40% of Basic, non metro) ₹4,200 Fixed, partially exempt


Special Allowance ₹5,500 Fixed, taxable


Conveyance Allowance ₹800 Fixed, taxable


**Gross Salary** **₹21,000**


**Employer Costs (Part of CTC)**


Employer PF (12% of Basic) ₹1,260 Statutory


Employer ESI (3.25% of Gross) ₹683 Statutory (gross ≤ ₹21,000)


EDLI + Admin (1% of Basic) ₹105 Statutory


Gratuity Provision (4.81% of Basic) ₹505 Statutory


Insurance ₹250 Benefit

**Total CTC** **₹23,803**

Employee ESI (0.75% of Gross) ₹158

**Total Deductions** **₹1,418**

**Take Home Percentage:** 78.3% of CTC

Meal Voucher ₹2,200 Tax free (with conditions)

Group Health Insurance ₹667 Benefit

### Structure 3: ₹15 LPA (₹1,25,000 Monthly CTC)


**Typical Role:** Senior developer, engineering manager, finance manager, AVP


Component Monthly Amount Type


**Earnings**

**Employer Costs**


Employer PF (12% of Basic) ₹6,240 Statutory

Group Health Insurance ₹1,500 Benefit

**Total Employer Cost** **₹11,014**

Metric ₹3 LPA ₹6 LPA ₹15 LPA


Monthly CTC ₹25,000 ₹50,000 ₹1,25,000

**Key Insight:** The take home percentage drops at higher CTC levels because TDS increases substantially. At ₹15 LPA, income tax alone takes approximately ₹8,500 per month.


## How to Design a Salary Structure (Employer Guide)


If you are a business owner or HR professional setting up salary structures for your team, follow this step by step approach:


### Step 1: Start with CTC


Decide the total annual cost you are willing to spend on the employee. This is your CTC budget.


### Step 2: Set Basic at 50% of Gross


With the Code on Wages requiring Basic + DA to be at least 50%, set basic at 50% of the estimated gross salary. If you do not pay DA separately, basic alone must be 50%.


### Step 3: Calculate Employer Statutory Costs


Component Formula


Employer PF 12% of Basic


EDLI + Admin 1% of Basic


Employer ESI 3.25% of Gross (only if gross ≤ ₹21,000)


Gratuity 4.81% of Basic


### Step 4: Calculate Gross Salary


Gross Salary = CTC minus all employer costs (PF, ESI, EDLI, gratuity, insurance)


### Step 5: Structure Gross into Components


Component Recommended Percentage of Basic


HRA 50% of Basic (metro) or 40% (non metro)


Special Allowance Remaining balance after all other components


Conveyance ₹1,600 fixed


Meal Voucher ₹2,200 (optional, tax effective)


Telephone Reimbursement ₹1,000 to ₹1,250 (optional, for roles needing phone usage)


NPS Employer (optional) 10% to 14% of Basic (excellent tax benefit under both regimes)


### Step 6: Verify Compliance


Check What to Verify


50% rule Basic + DA ≥ 50% of total remuneration


PF calculation PF is on Basic + DA (not on special allowance)


ESI threshold If any employee’s gross is ≤ ₹21,000, ESI applies


Total deductions Total deductions should not exceed 50% of wages


Minimum wages Gross salary meets your state’s minimum wage for the relevant scheduled employment


### Common Salary Structure Mistakes Employers Make


Mistake Why It Is Wrong The Fix


Keeping Basic at 30% to save PF cost Violates 50% rule under Code on Wages Set Basic at 50% and factor the higher PF into CTC


Not including gratuity in CTC Gratuity is a real cost that hits when employees complete 5 years Always include gratuity provision (4.81% of Basic) in CTC calculations


Same structure for all salary levels ESI, TDS, and tax benefits vary significantly by salary range Create different structures for different salary brackets


Showing employer PF as part of gross salary Misleading to employees; inflates apparent salary Employer PF is a cost above gross, not part of it


Not offering meal vouchers or NPS Missing easy tax optimization for employees Include ₹2,200 meal vouchers and consider NPS employer contribution


No salary restructuring after Code on Wages Non compliance risk Review and update all salary structures for 50% compliance


## Old Tax Regime vs New Tax Regime: Impact on Salary Structure


The tax regime an employee chooses directly affects which salary components provide tax savings.


### Which Components Save Tax Under Each Regime


Component Old Regime Benefit New Regime Benefit


Basic Salary No benefit (fully taxable) No benefit (fully taxable)


HRA Partially exempt (Section 10(13A)) No exemption (fully taxable)


LTA Exempt for travel (Section 10(5)) No exemption


Employee PF Section 80C deduction up to ₹1,50,000 No Section 80C


Employer NPS Section 80CCD(2), up to 14% of Basic Section 80CCD(2) available


Meal Vouchers Exempt up to ₹2,200/month Exempt up to ₹2,200/month


Standard Deduction ₹50,000 ₹75,000


Professional Tax Deductible under Section 16(iii) Deductible under Section 16(iii)


### Which Regime Is Better by CTC Level


CTC Range Likely Better Regime Reason


Below ₹7 LPA New Regime Zero tax with rebate; no need for investment proofs


₹7 to ₹12 LPA New Regime (usually) Rebate covers most of the income; old regime needs significant deductions to match


₹12 to ₹20 LPA Depends on deductions Old regime wins if total deductions (80C + 80D + HRA + home loan) exceed ₹3.75 lakh


Above ₹20 LPA New Regime (usually) Lower slab rates offset the loss of exemptions in most cases


**Employer Tip:** Design salary structures that work well under both regimes. Components like employer NPS contribution (tax free under both) and meal vouchers (exempt under both) benefit all employees regardless of their regime choice.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### 1. What is the ideal salary structure for employees in India in 2026?


The ideal salary structure in India for 2026 follows the Code on Wages requirement: Basic + DA at 50% of total remuneration, HRA at 40% to 50% of Basic (depending on the city), meal vouchers at ₹2,200 per month, and the remaining amount as special allowance. For higher salary levels (above ₹10 LPA), including an employer NPS contribution of 10% to 14% of Basic adds significant tax savings for employees under both tax regimes.


### 2. What is the difference between CTC, gross salary, and net salary?


CTC (Cost to Company) is the total annual cost an employer bears, including gross salary plus employer PF, ESI, gratuity, insurance, and other benefits. Gross salary is the total earnings before deductions (basic + HRA + all allowances). Net salary (take home) is the amount credited to the bank after deducting employee PF, ESI, professional tax, TDS, and other deductions. For a ₹6 LPA CTC, gross salary is typically around ₹5.2 to ₹5.5 LPA, and take home is around ₹4.7 to ₹4.8 LPA.


### 3. Why do companies keep basic salary low?


Historically, companies kept basic salary at 30% to 40% of CTC to reduce the PF and gratuity burden, since both are calculated as a percentage of basic. A lower basic meant lower employer PF contribution (12% of basic), lower gratuity liability (4.81% of basic), and higher take home for employees (less PF deduction). However, the Code on Wages, 2019 now requires basic + DA to be at least 50% of total remuneration, making this practice non compliant.


### 4. How does the 50% basic pay rule under Code on Wages affect my salary?


Under the Code on Wages, 2019, basic pay plus dearness allowance must be at least 50% of total remuneration. If your current basic is less than 50%, your employer will need to restructure your salary. This means your PF contribution will increase (both employee and employer), your gratuity entitlement will be higher, and your take home salary may decrease slightly. However, your long term retirement benefits will improve significantly. The provision came into effect on November 21, 2025, and employers should have aligned their structures for FY 2026-27.


### 5. What is HRA and how is HRA exemption calculated?


HRA (House Rent Allowance) is a salary component paid to employees for rental accommodation. The tax exemption is the lowest of three amounts: (a) actual HRA received, (b) 50% of basic in metro cities or 40% in non metro cities, and (c) actual rent paid minus 10% of basic salary. This exemption is available only under the old tax regime. Under the new tax regime, the entire HRA is taxable. To claim the exemption, employees must submit rent receipts and the landlord’s PAN if annual rent exceeds ₹1 lakh.


### 6. Should I choose the old or new tax regime based on my salary structure?


The new tax regime is generally better for employees with CTC below ₹12 lakh (zero tax with rebate) or above ₹20 lakh (lower slab rates compensate for lost deductions). The old regime works better if your total deductions (Section 80C + 80D + HRA exemption + home loan interest) exceed approximately ₹3.75 lakh per year. Since the new regime is the default from AY 2024-25, you must actively opt out if you want the old regime. Most employees below ₹12 LPA benefit from staying with the new regime.


### 7. Is dearness allowance (DA) paid in private companies?


DA is not common in private sector companies. It is primarily paid by central and state governments and public sector undertakings, where it is revised twice a year based on the Consumer Price Index. Most private companies adjust for inflation through annual salary increments or performance based raises rather than a separate DA component. However, under the Code on Wages, if a company does pay DA, it is added to basic for PF calculation purposes and counts toward the 50% threshold.


### 8. How should a small business owner decide the salary structure for new hires?


Start with the CTC budget for the role. Set basic at 50% of estimated gross salary to comply with the Code on Wages. Calculate employer costs (PF at 12%, gratuity at 4.81%, ESI at 3.25% if applicable, and insurance). Subtract employer costs from CTC to get gross salary. Then split gross into components: HRA at 40% to 50% of basic, meal vouchers at ₹2,200, and the balance as special allowance.
